name: Strasserism
summary: Strasserism is the 'German Socialism' of Otto Strasser and, in its 1925-26 program, his brother Gregor: a radical nationalist current inside and then against the Nazi Party. It combined anti-capitalist rhetoric, state supreme ownership of land with hereditary leases, estate chambers in place of parliament, and a racial nationalism that excluded Jews from citizenship, while rejecting Marxism and class struggle.
scope: Otto Strasser's doctrine as set out in the 1925-26 Strasser Program, the Fourteen Theses and the Black Front (1930-33), plus his memoir Hitler and I. Gregor Strasser's pragmatic 1932 economic proposals and the neo-Strasserism of later 'Third Position' groups are excluded except where noted.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Inferred from the proposed compulsory national life insurance with a state-guaranteed minimum for those unable to work.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from the pro-worker, profit-sharing economics; no wage-floor policy is documented.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Rejects 'capitalism' as monopolized property and puts land and resources under state supreme ownership, while keeping private credit and guilds.

public-ownership.rationale: The 1925-26 program nationalized key industries and the Fourteen Theses claimed supreme state ownership of land and resources.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from anti-capitalist, anti-monopoly stance; no tax program is documented for the Black Front strand.

unions-good.rationale: Favoured Nazi-style unions and worker profit-sharing within estates; inferred support for organized labor inside the national framework.

property-fundamental.rationale: Called for abolishing private ownership of land and means of production in favour of state ownership and hereditary leases.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Opposed monopolized capital, wanted heavy industry broken into small units and profits shared with workers and the state.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred from state-guaranteed minimum and social insurance proposals.

worker-ownership.rationale: Profit shares go to workers but managers receive the larger share and the state holds supreme ownership, so workers do not own firms collectively.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from an authoritarian conception of the state with concentrated executive power.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from a traditionalist, Christian-leaning nationalism; not addressed.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's own rhetoric included antisemitism, and it rejected liberal speech protections as part of the 'bureaucrats' democracy'.

strong-leader.rationale: Proposed a life-term elected president with concentrated power, though Otto insisted the Leader serves the Idea and can err.

state-harmful.rationale: Proposed a strong, authoritarian state organized in estates; no anti-statist strand.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred from authoritarian nationalism and ex-soldier base of the Black Front.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from traditionalist outlook; not addressed.

decide-locally.rationale: Rejected the totalitarian idea in favour of federalism: Swiss-style cantons or 15 regions and dissolution of Prussia.

rehabilitation.rationale: Proposed restitution and banishment in place of existing punishment; neither purely rehabilitative nor purely retributive.

traditional-family.rationale: Inferred from agrarian, hereditary-tenure society and later Christian emphasis.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from traditionalist, Christian-leaning outlook.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from nationalist and Christian outlook.

more-religion-public.rationale: Early writing was anti-clerical but later work made Christian values central ('without Christianity Europe is lost').

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred from the racial nationalism and the program's treatment of Jews as a pariah group.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from traditionalist outlook.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: German national renewal and protection of the 'German soul' were central.

gradual-change.rationale: Framed itself as a 'German Revolution' and wanted radical restructuring rather than gradual reform.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The 1925-26 program called for expelling Jewish immigrants who arrived after 1914.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Nationalist and wary of supranational bodies, though it envisioned a European federation under German leadership.

free-trade.rationale: Proposed replacing international finance with a barter economy and a self-contained European sphere.

nation-first.rationale: Otto held a good German politician must put Germany's good first, tempered by a European federation idea.

open-borders.rationale: Programmatic demands to expel and exclude, and to strip citizenship from German Jews.

limit-growth.rationale: Anti-industrial and agrarian, but not motivated by environmental limits.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The sources document no position on this question.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Romantic, anti-industrial outlook per scholars; inferred.

revolution-justified.rationale: Called its project the 'German Revolution' and the Black Front the school of its officers; Otto wanted to avoid strangling the social revolution for legality.

experts-over-public.rationale: Elites were to be selected through service and education and sit in estate chambers rather than parliament.

central-planning.rationale: Favoured guilds, small enterprise and decentralized industry over central planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Accepts guild and small-enterprise markets under state ownership of land and resources; inferred.

land-value-tax.rationale: State supreme ownership of land with leases, but no tax scheme documented.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Hereditary fiefs are inheritable; no inheritance-tax position documented.

basic-income.rationale: Emphasized work, compulsory labor service, and minimum only for those unable to work.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Inferred from barter economy and autarkic, regionally closed economic thinking.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State held supreme ownership, and Gregor's 1932 program centered on public works.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Broke up estates, favoured guilds and small enterprise, decentralized industry and a de-proletarianized hereditary-tenure peasantry.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Retained wage labor, interest-bearing credit and profit shares.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Wanted to supplant international finance, but with state oversight, not market money.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The program organized society in estates with corporate chambers and profit-sharing among state, managers and workers.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Black Front aimed at a cadre-led revolutionary movement guided by 'the Idea'; inferred.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Proposed a life-term elected president, although monarchists joined the Black Front.

democracy-best.rationale: Denounced Weimar as a 'hypocritical facade' and proposed 'authoritarian democracy' with estate chambers.

direct-votes.rationale: Inferred from rejection of parliamentary forms in favour of estates and a strong president.

workers-councils.rationale: Replaced class with estates and managers' primacy; chambers were corporate, not workers' councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: Federal regions inside one German state; inferred.

natural-rulers.rationale: Selection of elites through service framed as 'racial selection'; Gregor said people are unequal from birth.

political-violence-never.rationale: Revolutionary and paramilitary-linked movement; violence not ruled out.

war-builds-character.rationale: The Fourteen Theses called war the 'will of destiny' though Otto in memoir disclaimed war against France.

separate-church-state.rationale: Early anti-clericalism gave way to Christian emphasis; split.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Christian values central but no scriptural law program.

military-superiority.rationale: Inferred from demands for 1914 borders, colonies and living space.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Racial nationalism, danger of 'racial degeneration' and citizenship removal for Jews.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Replaced classes with estates and stood 'opposed to both Marxism and capitalism'.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Rejected egalitarianism; society organized by estates and merit.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Demanded colonies and a European colonial company.

civilizational-union.rationale: Proposed a European Federation and a 'White Europe', excluding Russia.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Subordinated individual interest to nation and estate; rejected capitalism.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The sources document no position on this question.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred from agrarian expansion and living-space aims.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Opposed urban industrialism and wanted a de-proletarianized, decentralized, agrarian society; scholars call it a flight into the past.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from romantic, hierarchical outlook.

restore-past-order.rationale: Hereditary fiefs, estates and guilds draw on an idealized pre-industrial order, though presented as a revolution.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Otto insisted the program be decided before seizing power, rejecting Hitler's 'power first'.

direct-action.rationale: Wanted a revolutionary movement above electoral politics; inferred.

means-match-ends.rationale: The sources document no position on this question.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Wanted a hereditary peasant and craft economy, not foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Guilds, estates and managers imply specialized roles.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Rejected egalitarianism; profit shares rewarded roles, managers more.

production-for-use.rationale: Anti-capitalist critique of speculative profit, inferred.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Rejected Marxism; profit is shared among state, managers and workers.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Opposed Marxism and class rule; wanted estates.

collective-farming.rationale: Land held as individual hereditary fiefs.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Criticized capitalism but not on a Leninist theory of imperialism.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rights through estate and nation; citizenship removed from Jews.

conscription.rationale: Proposed compulsory labor service and voluntary military service as elite filters.

state-as-business.rationale: Rejects market logic for the state; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Otto held that no man is free who is not economically independent.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Fourteen Theses spoke of racial degeneration and racial selection, though Otto criticized Hitler's racial theory.

organic-representation.rationale: Parliament would represent corporations and estates, not parties.

total-state.rationale: Otto rejected the totalitarian idea for federalism, despite authoritarian elements.

national-rebirth.rationale: The 'German Revolution' to renew the nation after Versailles and Weimar.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Demanded 1914 borders, African colonies and eastern raw-material zones; Otto disclaimed revenge war in his memoir.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Fiefs resemble feudal tenure, but authority rests on an elected president and estates.

bound-labor.rationale: Hereditary tenure was meant to secure peasants' independence, not bind labor to a lord.

universal-morality.rationale: Later writing presented Christian values as central.

single-common-good.rationale: National questions treated as fixed principles beyond partisan compromise; parliament only administrative.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Otto later backed Zionism as a means of Jewish emigration.

revive-national-language.rationale: The sources document no position on this question.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Managers held the larger profit share and a managerial estate.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Gregor's 1932 program was public-works financed work creation.

economic-freedom.rationale: Inferred; rejected liberal capitalism and held that freedom requires economic independence.

rule-by-example.rationale: Relied on legal structures, banishment and an elected president.

national-self-determination.rationale: Nationalist, wanted abolition of Versailles and return to 1914 borders.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Compulsory labor service and minimum only for those unable to work.

class-collaboration.rationale: Estates and profit-sharing among state, managers and workers replaced class conflict.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Reverent toward inherited German culture and tradition.

dominated-front.rationale: Strasserists are described as pro-Soviet by some and anti-Bolshevik by others; the European Federation excluded Russia.

ban-interest.rationale: Kept interest-bearing credit and unsecured personal loans.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Jews would be a pariah class without civil rights, ineligible for leases.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Rejected class analysis of the state.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The sources document no position on this question.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Aimed to expel or exclude rather than assimilate.

proportional-representation.rationale: Parliamentary parties were to be replaced by estate chambers.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Condemned the Weimar system as a hypocritical bureaucrats' democracy.

night-watchman-state.rationale: State owned land and resources and directed the economy.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Marriage to a foreigner would end German citizenship; fears of racial degeneration.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Talk of racial degeneration and racial selection, inferred.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Unequal from birth (Gregor) and citizenship stripped from Jews.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Favoured colonies and a settlement program in the East.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Proposed replacing the Civil Code; no position on religious law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The sources document no position on this question.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: The sources document no position on this question.

trade-surplus.rationale: Inferred from autarkic, economic nationalist outlook.

population-transfer.rationale: Expelling post-1914 Jewish immigrants and reclassifying German Jews as foreign.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Fourteen Theses framed war and struggle as destiny.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed; the Black Front was itself banned in 1933.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Otto held economic independence is a condition of freedom.

separated-powers.rationale: Checks and balances were largely nominal under the proposed presidency.

vanguard-party.rationale: The Black Front described itself as the officer school of the revolution.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Not addressed; the program favoured state ownership of land with hereditary leases and widespread small property, which neither clearly supports nor opposes selling public housing.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred from the corporatist estate-chamber model and the rejection of class struggle, though Otto Strasser criticised Hitler's treatment of workers.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Inferred from the anti-capitalist claim that poverty comes from finance capital and property relations, though the program also stressed living space for Germany.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The program was a racial nationalism that excluded Jews from citizenship and held that a national community rests on shared descent.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Inferred from the estate chambers and leader-selection by service and rank, which are the opposite of chance selection.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred from the authoritarian leadership principle and rejection of liberal parliamentarism, though Strasser opposed Hitler's dictatorship.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Inferred from the state-directed national economy and the plan to subordinate private interest to the community.

party-controls-media.rationale: No documented position; the program pushed authoritarian nationalism but Otto Strasser demanded press freedom in exile and in the Black Front.

party-commands-army.rationale: Inferred from Strasser's break with Hitler's SA-based party army and his support for a national army outside party control.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The program made citizenship depend on descent and proposed treating Jews as foreigners, implying restrictive naturalisation.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Inferred from the anti-capitalist, service-to-the-nation ethos of German Socialism; no program line on official pay.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Inferred from the Black Front as a leader-led cadre movement that demanded loyalty to its program.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Inferred from Strasser's proposals for a European federation of nations, which he saw as compatible with nationalism; contested.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Inferred from his rejection of parliament in favour of estate chambers and a strong leader.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Strasser wanted a national Christian culture but his program gives no ruling on church governance, so this is left neutral.

clerical-rule.rationale: His state was a secular racial-national one run by estate chambers and a leader, with no role for clerical authority.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: He rejected Marxism and class struggle and put the nation first, so workers owed their own state loyalty, not its defeat.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred from the cultural-nationalist demand that art and press serve the German nation and its character.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred from his preference for a strong leader over parliament, which implies no term limits; no explicit source.

recall-officials.rationale: His estate-chamber model replaced elections as such and the program is silent on recall, so adherents have no clear answer.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Inferred from Strasser's anti-Western, anti-Versailles stance and calls for a European federation; documentation is thin.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Land is held as inheritable state fiefs by those who work it, but rented housing is not discussed.

people-in-arms.rationale: Not clearly addressed; the movement favoured strong paramilitary organisation but its army policy is not documented.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on a land-bound peasantry and hereditary holdings.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Inferred from the pan-German nationalism that sought a single German state.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Inferred from the populist, anti-bourgeois rhetoric; no explicit statement found.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Inferred from the racial nationalism that ranked peoples; Strasser's own statements were more nuanced.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from the authoritarian state-centred program; not specifically documented.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist, organic-community outlook; not addressed.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; Strasser was critical of churches but no creationism policy is documented.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from the moralising, community-first nationalism.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The program restricted citizenship to those of German descent and excluded Jews.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred from the racial-nationalist conception of a single German people.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The program excluded Jews from citizenship and subordinated individuals to the national community, so exemptions are inferred as opposed.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred from the organic national community and estate order, which subordinated individuals to the whole.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Inferred from the anti-finance-capital, anti-"interest slavery" stance; poor-country debt itself is not addressed.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine joining national liberation with a socialist reordering of ownership.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Inferred from the plan to replace parliament with estate chambers, so an elected constituent assembly is not the favoured route.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Inferred from the authoritarian-nationalist state the program envisaged; Strasser also opposed Hitler's dictatorship, so this is contested.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred from the racial-nationalist focus on duties to the German nation rather than to the world's poor.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the demand for full German sovereignty against the Versailles order.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred from the estate-based state, which leaves little room for a popular presidential vote.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Inferred from the call for state control of credit and banking against finance capital.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist commitment to the historic German homeland and its borders.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Land and capital were held as state fiefs and property was bound to national service under the Strasser Program.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Strasser rejected Marxism yet sought ties with Russia; the USSR's character is not addressed, so adherents have no clear line.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred from the anti-industrial, land-rooted strand of German Socialism; the program does not address environmental risk.

collective-defense.rationale: Strasser rejected alignment with the Western powers and the League and sought a neutral Germany tied to the East.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from the demand to reunify Germany and recover lost territory; Strasser also opposed Hitler's later annexations.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Inferred: the program was Christian-leaning and rejected anti-clericalism, yet wanted state primacy; adherents are split.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred from the estates-based state, where the head of state stands above parties, which Strasser abolished.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from the strongly nationalist demand for German unity; the program does not discuss secession.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Inferred from the uniform corporate-state structure and hereditary state leases applied across Germany.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Strasser opposed restoring the monarchy and treated the state as secular and national, not dynastic or divine.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Strasser's anti-capitalist program favoured steeper burdens on wealth and large property over flat charges.

character-from-environment.rationale: Racial nationalism rests on innate national and racial character rather than upbringing.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred: Strasser denounced Hitler's arbitrary rule and wanted a state of estates bound by a constitution.

space-expansion.rationale: Inferred from the inward, agrarian and anti-capitalist focus; space was outside the program.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Inferred from the estate chambers combined with a leader, a blend of corporate and executive power.

leader-cult.rationale: Strasser broke with Hitler partly over the personal Fuhrer cult and denounced it in his memoir.

equal-parenting.rationale: Never addressed; adherents have no clear position on custody law.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Strasser rejected class struggle and proposed replacing classes with vocational estates.

land-redistribution.rationale: The program broke up large estates, vesting ultimate ownership in the nation and leasing land to farmers as hereditary fiefs.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from racial nationalism that excluded Jews and stressed a homogeneous German nation; return was not discussed.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The program demanded the 1914 borders and an ethnic-nationalist German state, which implies some claim on German-inhabited land.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred: he proposed Christian-only franchise in drafts but not a punishment for apostasy.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from his traditional estates-based social model that rejected feminism, but compulsion by law is not documented.

common-currency.rationale: Inferred from his aim of replacing international finance with a barter economy under state foreign-trade monopoly.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: He proposed a European federation and later White Christian federations, which suggests kin-based unions.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred: he stripped Jews of citizenship rather than granting self-governing cultural institutions.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The program removed Jewish citizenship and Strasser later supported Zionism as a way to separate Jews from Germany, the opposite of staying and demanding equal rights.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Strasser rejected Marxism and historical materialism in favour of a nationalist and spiritual socialism.

ban-cartels.rationale: His motto was 'monopolies for no one, property for everyone', and heavy industry would be broken into small units.

no-bailouts.rationale: Inferred from his hostility to finance capital and demand for state control; bailouts are not discussed.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: He rejected both liberal checks and majority parliamentary rule in favour of estate chambers, so the question does not map.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from an estates-based order with traditional social roles; not addressed.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: He planned a state monopoly of foreign trade and a bloc with a European federation, though he rejected a 'Spartan' autarky.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred: he rejected international finance and liberal trade, and set aside binding international standards on sovereignty grounds.

moral-incentives.rationale: Inferred from his stress on labour service and duty to the national community.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; he opposed both Hitler's putschism and Marxist revolution, and organised the Black Front politically.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: He opposed the Junker aristocracy and wanted elites chosen by education and service, though land was inherited through male heirs.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Strasserism is a radical German nationalism that put the German nation and its folk culture at the centre of politics.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred from Otto Strasser's anti-imperialist rhetoric and his stress on national self-determination for each nation; he did not argue the point as such.

patriotic-education.rationale: As a nationalist movement it aimed to build national loyalty and pride, and it was a rival to Hitler's party on nationalist grounds.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from its racial nationalism, which favoured treating citizens by national belonging and not by aid to minority groups.

public-money-creation.rationale: Its program of state supremacy over land and finance and attacks on 'interest slavery' point to public control of money; inferred.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: It was anti-capitalist yet rejected Marxism and class struggle, so it did not rest on an inevitable collapse; inferred.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred from its nationalist vision of a German-led central European order, which implies influence over neighbouring lands.

delink-world-market.rationale: Inferred from its anti-capitalist, state-directed economy of a closed national bloc and distrust of world finance.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: It denied class struggle and spoke of a national community of workers, so it would not split rich-country workers from the exploited.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: It put land and economy under state supremacy and estates, so it rejects absolute private freedom to deal with whomever one likes.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Its estate chambers replaced parliament, and it subordinated individual rights to the national community; inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred: he demanded the return of colonies and 1914 borders, so colonial-era arrangements were not treated as void.

elective-rulers.rationale: He proposed a life-term president elected rather than a hereditary head of state.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from the authoritarian estates order, which put the whole above individual consent.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred: the Black Front rejected Hitler as a betrayer of the movement, but no doctrine of lawful resistance is documented.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Estate chambers were to replace parliament, and he denounced Weimar parliamentarism as a facade.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: The sources document no position on animals.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The sources document no position on animals.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred from the paternal, state-guaranteed minimum and the managers' and estates' duties to the national community.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: A political movement leader whose doctrine called for active national renewal, not retreat.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from his hostility to Marxist cultural analysis and stress on national will.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian thesis he did not hold; inferred from his rejection of Marxist class analysis.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred from his denunciation of international finance and the Versailles burden on Germany.

native-born-offices.rationale: The program reserved citizenship, and with it public office, to Germans of German blood.

party-own-road.rationale: Inferred: an anti-Marxist nationalist who sought ties with Russia but rejected direction from any foreign party.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: He proposed a self-contained economic sphere and barter in place of international finance.

return-lost-territory.rationale: He demanded abolition of Versailles and a return to the 1914 borders.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred; he favoured colonies and an eastern settlement program, which set settlers above natives.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred: a racial nationalist who broke with Hitler over strategy and socialism, not over antifascism.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred: he rejected Marxism but also sought an authoritarian national order, so he would not join in condemning both as equivalent.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed; the sources document no position.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from reverence for German tradition and national memory.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed; the sources document no position.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed; the sources document no position.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from his rejection of Weimar as an alien parliamentary system and his estates model of German socialism.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred from the ex-soldier base of the Black Front and authoritarian nationalism.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from the traditional, hereditary-tenure social order.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from the movement's conservative, organic national community and emphasis on family.

office-by-exam.rationale: Strasser replaced parliament with estate chambers drawn from vocations, which is neither election by party nor examination; the program does not settle this.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The program puts key industries under state or national control against international capital.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the program's völkisch family policy aimed at preserving the nation.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Strasser rejected parliamentary representation in favour of estates and a leader, with no recall by voters.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from the proposed compulsory national insurance with state-guaranteed minimum.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The program makes the state ultimate owner of land and grants it to citizens on hereditary lease, which can be withdrawn for misuse.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Strasser rejected parliamentary government, so budget control by an elected parliament is not part of his scheme.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from its German nationalism and nation-state focus.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from land held by state and leased to citizens of the German nation; foreigners are excluded from citizenship.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from its racial nationalism, which treats group differences as natural rather than as discrimination.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from its anti-capitalist, anti-materialist critique of liberal society.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from its anti-Versailles nationalism and tolerance of covert action for German aims.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from Strasser's vision of a German-led Europe in the Black Front.

corporate-influence.rationale: The Strasser program attacked big capital and finance as dominating the state, in line with its anti-capitalist rhetoric.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from its extreme nationalism and hostility to foreign capital and influence over Germany.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from its racial nationalism and völkisch concern for the nation's biological strength; no specific policy found in the sources.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from the program's state-owned land leased only to citizens on hereditary terms, which excludes outsiders.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from the state-led economy and Gregor Strasser's 1932 work-creation plan, though no formal guarantee was proposed.

democratic-peace.rationale: It rejected parliamentary democracy for estate chambers and held a nationalist view of war and international relations.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: It stressed a strong, organic state and national duty over individual choice.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred from its nationalist stress on German sovereignty and rejection of Versailles-era Western interference.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred from the estate-chamber corporatism that organised workers by occupational estate within the state, not craft unions.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The program excluded Jews from citizenship and the movement held antisemitic views, though Otto Strasser later softened them.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from its conservative nationalism and family-centred völkisch ideals.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from its authoritarian leadership principle; Strasser's Black Front demanded press freedom only against Hitler.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from its autarkic German socialism and hereditary land ties, favouring national self-sufficiency over world trade.

informal-organisation.rationale: It built a disciplined, hierarchical movement (the Black Front) around leadership and estate organisation.

national-law-over-international.rationale: It was radically nationalist and rejected Versailles and international constraints on German sovereignty.

religious-nation.rationale: Its nation was defined by race and blood rather than religion, though it was nominally Christian.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from radical nationalism and opposition to Western dominance, which favours sovereign equality of nations.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Not addressed; the program was centralist on land and economy but also federal, so adherents could split.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred from the program, which put land under state supreme ownership with hereditary leases while keeping other property in private hands.

defeat-communism.rationale: Strasser opposed Marxism at home but favoured ties with Soviet Russia against the West, so defeat of communism was not a stated aim.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from estate chambers and state-directed economy that favours state or corporate control of services.

religion-illusion.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from rejection of Marxism and a nationalist, Christian-leaning outlook.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The program rejected capitalism and denounced it as exploitative, calling for German Socialism instead.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the program's traditional, family-centred nationalism.

socialized-care.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the program's emphasis on the family and a rejection of Marxist collectivism.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from radical German nationalism, which favoured cultural purity.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from racial nationalism that excluded Jews from citizenship and had no concept of binding minority treaties.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred from the program's estate chambers and national economy, which rest on the nation-state rather than small communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from racial nationalism that favoured a unified German nation.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: German Socialism was presented as a third course between capitalism and Marxism, rejecting both.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Ethnic nationalists put the nation's attachment to land first; Strasser opposed Hitler's eastern expansion but still held völkisch views; inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not sourced; Otto Strasser broke with Hitler and later neo-Strasserists vary, so this is an inference only.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from traditional morality and the German law of his time.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Strasserism backs a strong one-party national state, so suppressing opposition is inferred.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Not addressed; Strasser wanted a national Christian-influenced culture without theocracy.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Strasser sought German national liberation against Versailles and opposed imperialism, so an extractive empire is not his aim; inferred.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; sympathy with national resistance but no concern with Islamic duty.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Not addressed; Strasserists are not religious-law politicians.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Strasserism favoured a corporatist, estate-based and authoritarian order rather than mass participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: It rejects class struggle and egalitarian framings in favour of national community.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from traditional, nationalist views.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from traditional Christian-influenced values.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Strasserism presents itself as national socialism above left and right, combining elements of both.

alienated-labor.rationale: Strasser attacked capitalism and wage dependence in favour of German socialism; inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred from ethnic nationalism and opposition to immigration.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Not addressed; Christianity valued as culture but authority from the nation.

social-market-economy.rationale: Strasserism wanted a corporatist, state-supervised economy with social protection, which resembles this description; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Strasserism glorifies the nation and military strength and rejects pacifism.

rich-first.rationale: Strasserism favoured broad small property and state-regulated economy; inferred as opposing sharp inequalities.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Strasser sought Germany's independence from the western powers and an orientation toward a neutral Europe; inferred.

missingStatements.text: The state should hold ultimate ownership of all land and lease it to citizens on hereditary terms.
missingStatements.rationale: Central to the Fourteen Theses and Strasser Program: land held as inheritable state fiefs.

notes: The Strasser brothers differed: Gregor was a pragmatic party organizer who dropped anti-capitalist rhetoric by late 1932, and historians doubt Otto's postwar self-portrait as a principled socialist. Several answers are low-confidence inferences.
